sanskrit: atha tasmin nimittāni dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇapūrvajaḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmisaṃpannam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then, having observed those omens, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa spoke these words to the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: parigṛhyodakaṃ śītaṃ vanāni phalavanti ca balaughaṃ saṃvibhajyemaṃ vyūhya tiṣṭhema lakṣmaṇa
english: "Having secured cool water and fruit-bearing forests, let us divide our masses of troops, array them in formation, and stand ready, O Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: lokakṣayakaraṃ bhīmaṃ bhayaṃ paśyāmy upasthitam nibarhaṇaṃ pravīrāṇām ṛkṣavānararakṣasām
english: I see a terrible danger approaching—one that will bring destruction to the world—the slaughter of mighty warriors among bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas alike.

sanskrit: vātāś ca paruṣaṃ vānti kampate ca vasuṃdharā parvatāgrāṇi vepante patanti dharaṇīdharāḥ
english: The winds blow harshly, the earth quakes, the mountain peaks tremble, and great hills come crashing down.

sanskrit: meghāḥ kravyādasaṃkāśāḥ paruṣāḥ paruṣasvanāḥ krūrāḥ krūraṃ pravarṣanti miśraṃ śoṇitabindubhiḥ
english: Clouds resembling carrion-eaters, harsh and harsh-sounding, rain down cruelly, mixed with drops of blood.

sanskrit: raktacandanasaṃkāśā saṃdhyāparamadāruṇā jvalac ca nipataty etad ādityād agnimaṇḍalam
english: The twilight glow is exceedingly dreadful, resembling red sandalwood, and a blazing disc of fire falls from the sun.

sanskrit: ādityam abhivāśyante janayanto mahad bhayam dīnā dīnasvarā ghorā apraśastā mṛgadvijāḥ
english: Wild beasts and birds, wretched and mournful in voice, cry toward the sun, portending great terror—they are inauspicious and grim.

sanskrit: rajanyām aprakāśaś ca saṃtāpayati candramāḥ kṛṣṇaraktāṃśuparyanto yathā lokasya saṃkṣaye
english: At night the moon burns without proper light, its rays bordered with black and red, as at the dissolution of the world.

sanskrit: hrasvo rūkṣo 'praśastaś ca pariveṣaḥ sulohitaḥ ādityamaṇḍale nīlaṃ lakṣma lakṣmaṇa dṛśyate
english: The solar halo is small, rough, inauspicious, and intensely red; and a dark mark is seen on the disc of the sun, O Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: dṛśyante na yathāvac ca nakṣatrāṇy abhivartate yugāntam iva lokasya paśya lakṣmaṇa śaṃsati
english: The stars do not appear as they should, and the moment at hand portends, as it seems, the end of an age for the world—behold, Lakṣmaṇa!

sanskrit: kākāḥ śyenās tathā gṛdhrā nīcaiḥ paripatanti ca śivāś cāpy aśivā vācaḥ pravadanti mahāsvanāḥ
english: Crows, hawks, and vultures wheel low overhead, and jackals cry with great voices—but their cries are inauspicious omens.

sanskrit: kṣipram adya durādharṣāṃ purīṃ rāvaṇapālitām abhiyāma javenaiva sarvato haribhir vṛtāḥ
english: Therefore, swiftly today let us advance upon that city difficult to assail, the city guarded by Rāvaṇa, surrounding it on all sides with our monkey forces."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ tu vadan vīro lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ tasmād avātarac chīghraṃ parvatāgrān mahābalaḥ
english: Saying these words to Lakṣmaṇa, the mighty elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa—that hero of great strength—swiftly descended from the mountain summit.

sanskrit: avatīrya tu dharmātmā tasmāc chailāt sa rāghavaḥ paraiḥ paramadurdharṣaṃ dadarśa balam ātmanaḥ
english: Having descended from that mountain, the righteous-souled Rāghava reviewed his own army, which was utterly difficult for the enemy to assail.

sanskrit: saṃnahya tu sasugrīvaḥ kapirājabalaṃ mahat kālajño rāghavaḥ kāle saṃyugāyābhyacodayat
english: Then Rāghava, who knew the right moment, girded himself together with Sugrīva, and at the proper time urged the vast army of the monkey king forward to battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāle mahābāhur balena mahatā vṛtaḥ prasthitaḥ purato dhanvī laṅkām abhimukhaḥ purīm
english: Then the long-armed archer, surrounded by his great force, marched forth at the right hour, moving to the fore, his face turned toward the city of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: taṃ vibhīṣaṇa sugrīvau hanūmāñ jāmbavān nalaḥ ṛkṣarājas tathā nīlo lakṣmaṇaś cānyayus tadā
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, Sugrīva, Hanūmān, Jāmbavān, Nala, the king of bears, Nīla, and Lakṣmaṇa all followed him then.

sanskrit: tataḥ paścāt sumahatī pṛtanarkṣavanaukasām pracchādya mahatīṃ bhūmim anuyāti sma rāghavam
english: Then behind them followed the vast army of bears and forest-dwelling monkeys, covering the great earth as they went, following Rāghava.

sanskrit: śailaśṛṅgāṇi śataśaḥ pravṛddhāṃś ca mahīruhān jagṛhuḥ kuñjaraprakhyā vānarāḥ paravāraṇāḥ
english: The monkeys, mighty as elephants and rivals of the greatest elephants, seized by the hundreds mountain peaks and great full-grown trees.

sanskrit: tau tv adīrgheṇa kālena bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau rāvaṇasya purīṃ laṅkām āsedatur ariṃdamau
english: Within a short time those two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa—tamers of foes—had reached Laṅkā, the city of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: patākāmālinīṃ ramyām udyānavanaśobhitām citravaprāṃ suduṣprāpām uccaprākāratoraṇām
english: That city, beautiful with its garlands of banners, adorned with gardens and groves, with variegated ramparts, exceedingly difficult to approach, with lofty walls and gateways—

sanskrit: tāṃ surair api durdharṣāṃ rāmavākyapracoditāḥ yathānideśaṃ saṃpīḍya nyaviśanta vanaukasaḥ
english: —that city difficult to assail even for the gods: urged by Rāma's command, the forest-dwellers encircled it in their assigned positions and encamped.

sanskrit: laṅkāyās tūttaradvāraṃ śailaśṛṅgam ivonnatam rāmaḥ sahānujo dhanvī jugopa ca rurodha ca
english: Rāma, the archer, together with his younger brother, guarded and blockaded the northern gate of Laṅkā, which rose high like a mountain peak.

sanskrit: laṅkām upaniviṣṭaś ca rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ lakṣmaṇānucaro vīraḥ purīṃ rāvaṇapālitām
english: And Rāma, son of Daśaratha, that hero attended by Lakṣmaṇa, having encamped around Laṅkā, kept watch over the city ruled by Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: uttaradvāram āsādya yatra tiṣṭhati rāvaṇaḥ nānyo rāmād dhi tad dvāraṃ samarthaḥ parirakṣitum
english: Taking his stand at the northern gate where Rāvaṇa himself was stationed—for none other than Rāma was capable of guarding that gate.

sanskrit: rāvaṇādhiṣṭhitaṃ bhīmaṃ varuṇeneva sāgaram sāyudhau rākṣasair bhīmair abhiguptaṃ samantataḥ laghūnāṃ trāsajananaṃ pātālam iva dānavaiḥ
english: That terrible gate held by Rāvaṇa—like the ocean held by Varuṇa—guarded on all sides by fearsome rākṣasas with weapons, strike terror into the timid as does Pātāla guarded by dānavas.

sanskrit: vinyastāni ca yodhānāṃ bahūni vividhāni ca dadarśāyudhajālāni tathaiva kavacāni ca
english: He saw arrayed there many varied masses of weapons belonging to the warriors, and likewise their armour.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ tu dvāram āsādya nīlo haricamūpatiḥ atiṣṭhat saha maindena dvividena ca vīryavān
english: At the eastern gate, Nīla, lord of the monkey host, valiant and mighty, took his stand together with Mainda and Dvivida.

sanskrit: aṅgado dakṣiṇadvāraṃ jagrāha sumahābalaḥ ṛṣabheṇa gavākṣeṇa gajena gavayena ca
english: Aṅgada, of immense strength, seized the southern gate, together with Ṛṣabha, Gavākṣa, Gaja, and Gavaya.

sanskrit: hanūmān paścimadvāraṃ rarakṣa balavān kapiḥ pramāthi praghasābhyāṃ ca vīrair anyaiś ca saṃgataḥ
english: The powerful monkey Hanūmān guarded the western gate, accompanied by Pramāthin, Praghasa, and other heroes.

sanskrit: madhyame ca svayaṃ gulme sugrīvaḥ samatiṣṭhata saha sarvair hariśreṣṭhaiḥ suparṇaśvasanopamaiḥ
english: In the central reserve Sugrīva himself took his stand, together with all the foremost monkeys who were like Garuḍa and the wind in speed.

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ tu ṣaṭtriṃśat koṭyaḥ prakhyātayūthapāḥ nipīḍyopaniviṣṭāś ca sugrīvo yatra vānaraḥ
english: Thirty-six crores of monkeys, renowned troop-leaders, massed and encamped there where the monkey Sugrīva had stationed himself.

sanskrit: śāsanena tu rāmasya lakṣmaṇaḥ savibhīṣaṇaḥ dvāre dvāre harīṇāṃ tu koṭiṃ koṭiṃ nyaveśayat
english: By Rāma's command, Lakṣmaṇa together with Vibhīṣaṇa stationed a crore of monkeys at each gate, gate by gate.

sanskrit: paścimena tu rāmasya sugrīvaḥ saha jāmbavān adūrān madhyame gulme tasthau bahubalānugaḥ
english: To the west of Rāma, Sugrīva along with Jāmbavān took his position not far away in the central reserve, followed by many forces.

sanskrit: te tu vānaraśārdūlāḥ śārdūlā iva daṃṣṭriṇaḥ gṛhītvā drumaśailāgrān hṛṣṭā yuddhāya tasthire
english: Those tiger-like monkeys, like tigers with their fangs, seized trees and mountain peaks and stood ready for battle with joy in their hearts.

sanskrit: sarve vikṛtalāṅgūlāḥ sarve daṃṣṭrānakhāyudhāḥ sarve vikṛtacitrāṅgāḥ sarve ca vikṛtānanāḥ
english: All had waving tails, all were armed with fangs and claws as weapons, all had strange and varied markings on their bodies, and all had formidable faces.

sanskrit: daśanāgabalāḥ ke cit ke cid daśaguṇottarāḥ ke cin nāgasahasrasya babhūvus tulyavikramāḥ
english: Some had the strength of ten elephants, some even ten times more than that; some equalled in valor a thousand elephants.

sanskrit: santi caughā balāḥ ke cit ke cic chataguṇottarāḥ aprameyabalāś cānye tatrāsan hariyūthapāḥ
english: Some had the strength of a flood in spate; some were yet a hundredfold greater; and other monkey troop-leaders present there had immeasurable strength.

sanskrit: adbhutaś ca vicitraś ca teṣām āsīt samāgamaḥ tatra vānarasainyānāṃ śalabhānām ivodgamaḥ
english: The gathering of those monkey armies there was wonderful and varied—like the swarming of locusts.

sanskrit: paripūrṇam ivākāśaṃ saṃchanneva ca medinī laṅkām upaniviṣṭaiś ca saṃpatadbhiś ca vānaraiḥ
english: The sky seemed completely filled and the earth seemed entirely covered by the monkeys as they encamped around Laṅkā and leapt about.

sanskrit: śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ pṛthag ṛkṣavanaukasām laṅkā dvārāṇy upājagmur anye yoddhuṃ samantataḥ
english: A hundred times a hundred thousand bears and forest-dwellers separately came to the gates of Laṅkā; others came from all sides eager to fight.

sanskrit: āvṛtaḥ sa giriḥ sarvais taiḥ samantāt plavaṃgamaiḥ ayutānāṃ sahasraṃ ca purīṃ tām abhyavartata
english: That mountain was surrounded on all sides by those leaping beings, and ten million thousands of them advanced upon that city.

sanskrit: vānarair balavadbhiś ca babhūva drumapāṇibhiḥ sarvataḥ saṃvṛtā laṅkā duṣpraveśāpi vāyunā
english: With mighty monkeys bearing trees, Laṅkā was hemmed in on all sides—impenetrable even to the wind.

sanskrit: rākṣasā vismayaṃ jagmuḥ sahasābhinipīḍitāḥ vānarair meghasaṃkāśaiḥ śakratulyaparākramaiḥ
english: The rākṣasas were struck with amazement when suddenly they were pressed in upon by monkeys resembling clouds in mass and equal to Indra in valor.

sanskrit: mahāñ śabdo 'bhavat tatra balaughasyābhivartataḥ sāgarasyeva bhinnasya yathā syāt salilasvanaḥ
english: A mighty roar arose there as the flood of troops advanced, like the sound of the waters of the ocean when it is breached.

sanskrit: tena śabdena mahatā saprākārā satoraṇā laṅkā pracalitā sarvā saśailavanakānanā
english: By that great sound, all of Laṅkā—with its ramparts and gateways, together with its mountains, forests, and groves—was set trembling.

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇaguptā sā sugrīveṇa ca vāhinī babhūva durdharṣatarā sarvair api surāsuraiḥ
english: That army, protected by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa and by Sugrīva, became more difficult to assail than by all gods and asuras combined.

sanskrit: rāghavaḥ saṃniveśyaivaṃ sainyaṃ svaṃ rakṣasāṃ vadhe saṃmantrya mantribhiḥ sārdhaṃ niścitya ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having thus deployed his army for the destruction of the rākṣasas, and having deliberated with his counsellors and resolved upon a course of action again and again—

sanskrit: ānantaryam abhiprepsuḥ kramayogārthatattvavit vibhīṣaṇasyānumate rājadharmam anusmaran aṅgadaṃ vālitanayaṃ samāhūyedam abravīt
english: —intent on immediate action, knowing the true import of orderly method, mindful of royal duty with Vibhīṣaṇa's consent, Rāghava summoned Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, and spoke thus:

sanskrit: gatvā saumya daśagrīvaṃ brūhi madvacanāt kape laṅghayitvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ bhayaṃ tyaktvā gatavyathaḥ
english: "Go, dear monkey, and speak these words of mine to the ten-necked one—leaping over the city of Laṅkā, free from fear, with no anxiety:

sanskrit: bhraṣṭaśrīkagataiśvaryamumūrṣo naṣṭacetanaḥ ṛṣīṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā
english: 'O you whose glory has departed, whose sovereignty is gone, who desires death, whose sense has been destroyed—you who have wronged sages, gods, gandharvas, and apsarases,

sanskrit: nāgānām atha yakṣāṇāṃ rājñāṃ ca rajanīcara yac ca pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mohād avaliptena rākṣasa
english: nāgas, yakṣas, and kings, O night-roaming rākṣasa—the evil you have done through delusion and arrogance—

sanskrit: nūnam adya gato darpaḥ svayambhū varadānajaḥ yasya daṇḍadharas te 'haṃ dārāharaṇakarśitaḥ daṇḍaṃ dhārayamāṇas tu laṅkādvare vyavasthitaḥ
english: —that arrogance born of the Self-Existent's boon has surely now departed. I—I who wield the rod of punishment, worn down by the abduction of my wife—stand bearing the rod of punishment at the gate of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: padavīṃ devatānāṃ ca maharṣīṇāṃ ca rākṣasa rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ gamiṣyasi mayā hataḥ
english: You shall go, O rākṣasa, slain by me, to the same realm as the gods, the great seers, and all the royal sages.

sanskrit: balena yena vai sītāṃ māyayā rākṣasādhama mām atikrāmayitvā tvaṃ hṛtavāṃs tad vidarśaya
english: O basest of rākṣasas, show now that strength and that māyā by which you carried off Sītā, eluding me.

sanskrit: arākṣasam imaṃ lokaṃ kartāsmi niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ na cec charaṇam abhyeṣi mām upādāya maithilīm
english: With my sharpened arrows I shall make this world free of rākṣasas—unless you come to me for refuge, bringing the daughter of Mithilā.

sanskrit: dharmātmā rakṣasāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃprāpto 'yaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ laṅkaiśvaryaṃ dhruvaṃ śrīmān ayaṃ prāpnoty akaṇṭakam
english: The righteous-souled Vibhīṣaṇa, the best of rākṣasas, who has come to me—he will surely and without hindrance obtain the prosperous sovereignty of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: na hi rājyam adharmeṇa bhoktuṃ kṣaṇam api tvayā śakyaṃ mūrkhasahāyena pāpenāvijitātmanā
english: For you—with your foolish counsellors, sinful and with self unconquered—cannot enjoy the kingdom through unrighteousness even for a moment.

sanskrit: yudhyasva vā dhṛtiṃ kṛtvā śauryam ālambya rākṣasa maccharais tvaṃ raṇe śāntas tataḥ pūto bhaviṣyasi
english: Or else, summoning your courage and holding fast to your valor, fight, O rākṣasa—slain in battle by my arrows, you shall then be purified.

sanskrit: yady āviśasi lokāṃs trīn pakṣibhūto manojavaḥ mama cakṣuṣpathaṃ prāpya na jīvan pratiyāsyasi
english: If you should enter the three worlds transformed to a bird and swift as thought, once you fall within sight of my eyes you shall not return alive.'"

sanskrit: bravīmi tvāṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ kriyatām aurdhvadekikam sudṛṣṭā kriyatāṃ laṅkā jīvitaṃ te mayi sthitam
english: "I speak words of counsel to you: perform your last rites, take a good look at Laṅkā—your life rests in my hands."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu tāreyo rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā jagāmākāśam āviśya mūrtimān iva havyavāṭ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma of untiring deeds, Aṅgada, son of Tārā, entered the sky and went forth like fire incarnate.

sanskrit: so 'tipatya muhūrtena śrīmān rāvaṇamandiram dadarśāsīnam avyagraṃ rāvaṇaṃ sacivaiḥ saha
english: In a moment the illustrious one had overflown and beheld Rāvaṇa seated calmly in his palace together with his ministers.

sanskrit: tatas tasyāvidūreṇa nipatya haripuṃgavaḥ dīptāgnisadṛśas tasthāv aṅgadaḥ kanakāṅgadaḥ
english: Then the foremost monkey Aṅgada, wearing golden armlets, alighted not far from him and stood like a blazing fire.

sanskrit: tad rāmavacanaṃ sarvam anyūnādhikam uttamam sāmātyaṃ śrāvayām āsa nivedyātmānam ātmanā
english: He made known his own identity, and then caused Rāvaṇa and his ministers to hear all of Rāma's excellent message, neither less nor more.

sanskrit: dūto 'haṃ kosalendrasya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ vāliputro 'ṅgado nāma yadi te śrotram āgataḥ
english: "I am a messenger of Rāma, lord of Kosala, of untiring deeds. I am named Aṅgada, son of Vālin—if that name has reached your ears.

sanskrit: āha tvāṃ rāghavo rāmaḥ kausalyānandavardhanaḥ niṣpatya pratiyudhyasva nṛśaṃsaṃ puruṣādhama
english: Rāma the Rāghava, increaser of Kausalyā's joy, says to you: 'Come out, O cruel lowest of men, and fight in return.'

sanskrit: hantāsmi tvāṃ sahāmātyaṃ saputrajñātibāndhavam nirudvignās trayo lokā bhaviṣyanti hate tvayi
english: 'I shall slay you together with your ministers, your sons, kinsmen, and relatives. With you slain, the three worlds shall be free of anxiety.'

sanskrit: devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām śatrum adyoddhariṣyāmi tvām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca kaṇṭakam
english: 'Today I shall extract you, who are the enemy and thorn of gods, dānavas, yakṣas, gandharvas, serpents, rākṣasas, and sages.'

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇasya caiśvaryaṃ bhaviṣyati hate tvayi na cet satkṛtya vaidehīṃ praṇipatya pradāsyasi
english: 'And Vibhīṣaṇa shall obtain sovereignty when you are slain—unless you honor the daughter of Videha and return her with due reverence.'"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ bruvāṇe haripuṃgave amarṣavaśam āpanno niśācaragaṇeśvaraḥ
english: As the foremost monkey spoke these harsh words, the lord of the night-roaming host fell prey to indignation.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa roṣatāmrākṣaḥ śaśāsa sacivāṃs tadā gṛhyatām eṣa durmedhā vadhyatām iti cāsakṛt
english: Then with eyes reddened by rage he commanded his ministers repeatedly: "Seize this fool! Kill him!"

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā dīptāgnisamatejasaḥ jagṛhus taṃ tato ghorāś catvāro rajanīcarāḥ
english: Hearing Rāvaṇa's words—he whose splendor matched blazing fire—four terrible night-roaming rākṣasas then seized Aṅgada.

sanskrit: grāhayām āsa tāreyaḥ svayam ātmānam ātmanā balaṃ darśayituṃ vīro yātudhānagaṇe tadā
english: That hero, son of Tārā, allowed himself to be seized in order to display his strength before the host of yātudhānas.

sanskrit: sa tān bāhudvaye saktān ādāya patagān iva prāsādaṃ śailasaṃkāśam utpāpātāṅgadas tadā
english: Seizing those four who were clinging to his two arms as though they were birds, Aṅgada leapt up with them to the palace, which was like a mountain.

sanskrit: te 'ntarikṣād vinirdhūtās tasya vegena rākṣasāḥ bhumau nipatitāḥ sarve rākṣasendrasya paśyataḥ
english: Shaken off in midair by his momentum, all those rākṣasas fell to the ground before the eyes of the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāsādaśikharaṃ śailaśṛṅgam ivonnatam tat paphāla tadākrāntaṃ daśagrīvasya paśyataḥ
english: Then the pinnacle of the palace, lofty as a mountain peak, shattered under his feet before the eyes of the ten-necked Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: bhaṅktvā prāsādaśikharaṃ nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ vinadya sumahānādam utpapāta vihāyasā
english: Having shattered the palace pinnacle, having made his name resound, and having roared a mighty roar, he leapt up into the sky.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tu paraṃ cakre krodhaṃ prāsādadharṣaṇāt vināśaṃ cātmanaḥ paśyan niḥśvāsaparamo 'bhavat
english: But Rāvaṇa burned with extreme anger at the violation of his palace, and foreseeing his own destruction, he fell to heavy sighing.

sanskrit: rāmas tu bahubhir hṛṣṭair ninadadbhiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ vṛto ripuvadhākāṅkṣī yuddhāyaivābhyavartata
english: Meanwhile Rāma, desirous of slaying the enemy, advanced toward battle, surrounded by many joyfully roaring monkeys.

sanskrit: suṣeṇas tu mahāvīryo girikūṭopamo hariḥ bahubhiḥ saṃvṛtas tatra vānaraiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ
english: And the mighty Suṣeṇa, that monkey resembling a mountain peak, was surrounded there by many monkeys who could change form at will.

sanskrit: caturdvārāṇi sarvāṇi sugrīvavacanāt kapiḥ paryākramata durdharṣo nakṣatrāṇīva candramāḥ
english: At Sugrīva's command, that invincible monkey ranged past all four gates, like the moon moving through the constellations.

sanskrit: teṣām akṣauhiṇiśataṃ samavekṣya vanaukasām laṅkām upaniviṣṭānāṃ sāgaraṃ cātivartatām
english: Having reviewed a hundred akṣauhiṇī battalions of the forest-dwellers encamped around Laṅkā, and having crossed the ocean—

sanskrit: rākṣasā vismayaṃ jagmus trāsaṃ jagmus tathāpare apare samaroddharṣād dharṣam evopapedire
english: —the rākṣasas were struck with wonder; some were seized with fear; yet others, excited by battle-ardor, felt only the excitement.

sanskrit: kṛtsnaṃ hi kapibhir vyāptaṃ prākāraparikhāntaram dadṛśū rākṣasā dīnāḥ prākāraṃ vānarīkṛtam
english: The wretched rākṣasas saw the entire space within rampart and moat filled with monkeys—the walls had become a wall of monkeys.

sanskrit: tasmin mahābhīṣaṇake pravṛtte kolāhale rākṣasarājadhānyām pragṛhya rakṣāṃsi mahāyudhāni yugāntavātā iva saṃviceruḥ
english: When that great and fearful tumult broke out in the city of the rākṣasa king, the rākṣasas seized their great weapons and moved about like winds at the end of an age.

sanskrit: tatas te rākṣasās tatra gatvā rāvaṇamandiram nyavedayan purīṃ ruddhāṃ rāmeṇa saha vānaraiḥ
english: Then those rākṣasas went to Rāvaṇa's palace and reported that the city had been blockaded by Rāma together with the monkeys.

sanskrit: ruddhāṃ tu nagarīṃ śrutvā jātakrodho niśācaraḥ vidhānaṃ dviguṇaṃ śrutvā prāsādaṃ so 'dhyarohata
english: Hearing that the city was blockaded, the night-roaming Rāvaṇa was seized with anger; having ordered the deployment redoubled, he climbed to the palace roof.

sanskrit: sa dadarśāvṛtāṃ laṅkāṃ saśailavanakānanām asaṃkhyeyair harigaṇaiḥ sarvato yuddhakāṅkṣibhiḥ
english: He saw Laṅkā with its mountains, forests, and groves completely surrounded on all sides by innumerable bands of monkeys eager for battle.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā vānaraiḥ sarvāṃ vasudhāṃ kavalīkṛtām kathaṃ kṣapayitavyāḥ syur iti cintāparo 'bhavat
english: Seeing the entire earth swallowed up by monkeys, he fell into deep thought as to how they might be destroyed.

sanskrit: sa cintayitvā suciraṃ dhairyam ālambya rāvaṇaḥ rāghavaṃ hariyūthāṃś ca dadarśāyatalocanaḥ
english: Having reflected at length and steadying himself with composure, Rāvaṇa with his wide eyes gazed upon Rāghava and the monkey troops.

sanskrit: prekṣato rākṣasendrasya tāny anīkāni bhāgaśaḥ rāghavapriyakāmārthaṃ laṅkām āruruhus tadā
english: As the lord of rākṣasas watched, those armies in their divisions climbed upon Laṅkā then, eager to please Rāghava.

sanskrit: te tāmravaktrā hemābhā rāmārthe tyaktajīvitāḥ laṅkām evāhyavartanta sālatālaśilāyudhāḥ
english: They—copper-faced, golden in hue, their lives surrendered for Rāma's sake—stormed Laṅkā itself, armed with sāla trees, palm trees, and boulders.

sanskrit: te drumaiḥ parvatāgraiś ca muṣṭibhiś ca plavaṃgamāḥ prāsādāgrāṇi coccāni mamantus toraṇāni ca
english: The leaping monkeys with trees, mountain peaks, and bare fists smashed the tall palace towers and the gateways.

sanskrit: pārikhāḥ pūrayanti sma prasannasalilāyutāḥ pāṃsubhiḥ parvatāgraiś ca tṛṇaiḥ kāṣṭhaiś ca vānarāḥ
english: The monkeys filled the moats—which had been full of clear water—with earth, mountain peaks, grass, and timber.

sanskrit: tataḥ sahasrayūthāś ca koṭiyūthāś ca yūthapāḥ koṭīśatayutāś cānye laṅkām āruruhus tadā
english: Then troop-leaders commanding a thousand troops each, and those commanding a crore each, and others commanding a hundred crore troops, all climbed upon Laṅkā.

sanskrit: kāñcanāni pramṛdnantas toraṇāni plavaṃgamāḥ kailāsaśikharābhāni gopurāṇi pramathya ca
english: The leaping monkeys crushed the golden gateways and destroyed the gopura towers, which resembled the peaks of mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: āplavantaḥ plavantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ laṅkāṃ tām abhyavartanta mahāvāraṇasaṃnibhāḥ
english: Leaping, bounding, and roaring, the monkeys—resembling great elephants—advanced upon Laṅkā.

sanskrit: jayaty atibalo rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ rājā jayati sugrīvo rāghaveṇābhipālitaḥ
english: "Victory to Rāma, supremely mighty! Victory to the great-armed Lakṣmaṇa! Victory to king Sugrīva, protected by Rāghava!"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ ghoṣayantaś ca garjantaś ca plavaṃgamāḥ abhyadhāvanta laṅkāyāḥ prākāraṃ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Shouting and roaring in this way, the monkeys who could take any form they wished rushed at the walls of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: vīrabāhuḥ subāhuś ca nalaś ca vanagocaraḥ nipīḍyopaniviṣṭās te prākāraṃ hariyūthapāḥ
english: Vīrabāhu, Subāhu, and Nala who ranged the forest—those monkey troop-leaders massed themselves and encamped against the rampart.

sanskrit: etasminn antare cakruḥ skandhāvāraniveśanam
english: In the meantime they established an encampment of the main divisions.

sanskrit: pūrvadvāraṃ tu kumudaḥ koṭibhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ āvṛtya balavāṃs tasthau haribhir jitakāśibhiḥ
english: The mighty Kumuda surrounded the eastern gate, taking his stand encircled by ten crores of monkeys who bore the look of conquerors.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇadvāram āgamya vīraḥ śatabaliḥ kapiḥ āvṛtya balavāṃs tasthau viṃśatyā koṭibhir vṛtaḥ
english: The heroic monkey Śatabali came to the southern gate; the mighty one took his stand there encircled by twenty crores.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaḥ paścimadvāraṃ gatas tārā pitā hariḥ āvṛtya balavāṃs tasthau ṣaṣṭi koṭibhir āvṛtaḥ
english: Suṣeṇa, the father of Tārā, that monkey, went to the western gate; the mighty one took his stand there surrounded by sixty crores.

sanskrit: uttaradvāram āsādya rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha āvṛtya balavāṃs tasthau sugrīvaś ca harīśvaraḥ
english: Rāma, together with the son of Sumitrā, took his stand at the northern gate, mighty and encircling it; and Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, stood there too.

sanskrit: golāṅgūlo mahākāyo gavākṣo bhīmadarśanaḥ vṛtaḥ koṭyā mahāvīryas tasthau rāmasya pārvataḥ
english: The great-bodied Golāṅgūla, and Gavākṣa of fearsome appearance—both mighty heroes—each surrounded by a crore, stood at Rāma's flank.

sanskrit: ṛṣkāṇāṃ bhīmavegānāṃ dhūmraḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ vṛtaḥ koṭyā mahāvīryas tasthau rāmasya pārśvataḥ
english: Dhūmra, destroyer of enemies, mightiest among the terrifyingly swift bears, surrounded by a crore, stood at Rāma's side.

sanskrit: saṃnaddhas tu mahāvīryo gadāpāṇir vibhīṣaṇaḥ vṛto yas tais tu sacivais tasthau tatra mahābalaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, fully armored, mighty and valiant, mace in hand, stood there surrounded by his ministers—that man of great strength.

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ samantāt parighāvanto rarakṣur harivāhinīm
english: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, and Gandhamādana ranged about on all sides, guarding the monkey army.

sanskrit: tataḥ kopaparītātmā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ niryāṇaṃ sarvasainyānāṃ drutam ājñāpayat tadā
english: Then Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, his soul consumed by rage, commanded the immediate march out of all his forces.

sanskrit: niṣpatanti tataḥ sainyā hṛṣṭā rāvaṇacoditāḥ samaye pūryamāṇasya vegā iva mahodadheḥ
english: Then the soldiers sallied forth joyfully, urged on by Rāvaṇa, like the surge of the great ocean at the moment of high tide.

sanskrit: etasminn antare ghoraḥ saṃgrāmaḥ samapadyata rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca yathā devāsure purā
english: In the meantime a terrible battle broke out between the rākṣasas and the monkeys, as of old between the gods and asuras.

sanskrit: te gadābhiḥ pradīptābhiḥ śaktiśūlaparaśvadhaiḥ nijaghnur vānarān ghorāḥ kathayantaḥ svavikramān
english: Those terrible rākṣasas, proclaiming their own valor, struck down the monkeys with blazing maces, lances, spears, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: tathā vṛkṣair mahākāyāḥ parvatāgraiś ca vānarāḥ rākṣasās tāni rakṣāṃsi nakhair dantaiś ca vegitāḥ
english: Likewise the great-bodied monkeys with trees and mountain peaks, and the rākṣasas with those same weapons—swift with claws and teeth—struck at one another.

sanskrit: rākṣasās tv apare bhīmāḥ prākārasthā mahīgatān bhiṇḍipālaiś ca khaḍgaiś ca śūlaiś caiva vyadārayan
english: Other fearsome rākṣasas standing on the ramparts tore apart those on the ground below with slings, swords, and spears.

sanskrit: vānarāś cāpi saṃkruddhāḥ prākārasthān mahīgatāḥ rākṣasān pātayām āsuḥ samāplutya plavaṃgamāḥ
english: And the monkeys too, greatly enraged—those on the ground—leapt up and hurled down the rākṣasas who stood on the ramparts.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulo māṃsaśoṇitakardamaḥ rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca saṃbabhūvādbhutopamāḥ
english: That tumultuous clash between the rākṣasas and monkeys, a quagmire of flesh and blood, was like nothing ever seen before—a wonder beyond compare.

sanskrit: yudhyatāṃ tu tatas teṣāṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahātmanām rakṣasāṃ saṃbabhūvātha balakopaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
english: Then, as those great-souled monkeys were fighting, there arose among the rākṣasas an extremely fierce surge of force and fury.

sanskrit: te hayaiḥ kāñcanāpīḍair dhvajaiś cāgniśikhopamaiḥ rathaiś cādityasaṃkāśaiḥ kavacaiś ca manoramaiḥ
english: With horses bearing golden trappings, with banners like flames of fire, with chariots brilliant as the sun, and with beautiful armor—

sanskrit: niryayū rākṣasavyāghrā nādayanto diśo daśa rākṣasā bhīmakarmāṇo rāvaṇasya jayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: —the tiger-like rākṣasas of fearful deeds marched out, making the ten directions resound, desiring victory for Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: vānarāṇām api camūr mahatī jayam icchatām abhyadhāvata tāṃ senāṃ rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpiṇām
english: The great army of monkeys, desiring victory, advanced against that army of rākṣasas who could take any form at will.

sanskrit: etasminn antare teṣām anyonyam abhidhāvatām rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca dvandvayuddham avartata
english: In the meantime, as they charged at one another—rākṣasas and monkeys—single combat broke out.

sanskrit: aṅgadenendrajit sārdhaṃ vāliputreṇa rākṣasaḥ ayudhyata mahātejās tryambakeṇa yathāndhakaḥ
english: Indrajit the rākṣasa, of great splendor, fought with Aṅgada son of Vālin, as Tryambaka once fought with Andhaka.

sanskrit: prajaṅghena ca saṃpātir nityaṃ durmarṣaṇo raṇe jambūmālinam ārabdho hanūmān api vānaraḥ
english: Saṃpāti fought with Prajaṅgha, ever fierce in battle; and Hanūmān the monkey took on Jambūmālin.

sanskrit: saṃgataḥ sumahākrodho rākṣaso rāvaṇānujaḥ samare tīkṣṇavegena mitraghnena vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa's younger brother—the rākṣasa of immense wrath—met in battle the swift and fierce Mitraghna.

sanskrit: tapanena gajaḥ sārdhaṃ rākṣasena mahābalaḥ nikumbhena mahātejā nīlo 'pi samayudhyata
english: The mighty Gaja fought along with the rākṣasa Tapana, while the greatly splendorous Nīla fought with Nikumbha.

sanskrit: vānarendras tu sugrīvaḥ praghasena samāgataḥ saṃgataḥ samare śrīmān virūpākṣeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: The monkey-lord Sugrīva came to blows with Praghasa, while the illustrious Lakṣmaṇa met Virūpākṣa in battle.

sanskrit: agniketuś ca durdharṣo raśmiketuś ca rākṣasaḥ suptaghno yajñakopaś ca rāmeṇa saha saṃgatāḥ
english: The invincible rākṣasas Agniketu and Raśmiketu, and Suptaghna and Yajñakopa, all came together against Rāma.

sanskrit: vajramuṣṭis tu maindena dvividenāśaniprabhaḥ rākṣasābhyāṃ sughorābhyāṃ kapimukhyau samāgatau
english: The two leading monkeys Mainda and Dvivida, that pair of dreadful rākṣasas Vajramuṣṭi and Aśaniprabha, came face to face with each other.

sanskrit: vīraḥ pratapano ghoro rākṣaso raṇadurdharaḥ samare tīkṣṇavegena nalena samayudhyata
english: The heroic, terrible, and war-indomitable rākṣasa Pratapana fought in battle with the swift and fierce Nala.

sanskrit: dharmasya putro balavān suṣeṇa iti viśrutaḥ sa vidyunmālinā sārdham ayudhyata mahākapiḥ
english: Suṣeṇa, renowned as the powerful son of Dharma, that great monkey fought along with Vidyunmālin.

sanskrit: vānarāś cāpare bhīmā rākṣasair aparaiḥ saha dvandvaṃ samīyur bahudhā yuddhāya bahubhiḥ saha
english: And other fearsome monkeys joined single combats in many forms with yet other rākṣasas—many engaging many.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt sumahad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca vīrāṇāṃ jayam icchatām
english: There was waged a great, tumultuous, hair-raising battle between the rākṣasas and monkeys—heroes all, each desiring victory.

sanskrit: harirākṣasadehebhyaḥ prasṛtāḥ keśaśāḍvalāḥ śarīrasaṃghāṭavahāḥ prasusruḥ śoṇitāpagāḥ
english: Rivers of blood flowed from the bodies of monkeys and rākṣasas, carrying masses of matted hair, bearing along heaps of bodies.

sanskrit: ājaghānendrajit kruddho vajreṇeva śatakratuḥ aṅgadaṃ gadayā vīraṃ śatrusainyavidāraṇam
english: Indrajit, enraged, struck the hero Aṅgada—destroyer of enemy armies—with his mace, as Śatakratu might strike with the vajra.

sanskrit: tasya kāñcanacitrāṅgaṃ rathaṃ sāśvaṃ sasārathim jaghāna samare śrīmān aṅgado vegavān kapiḥ
english: Then the illustrious and swift monkey Aṅgada struck in battle Indrajit's chariot—golden and of splendid markings—together with its horses and charioteer.

sanskrit: saṃpātis tu tribhir bāṇaiḥ prajaṅghena samāhataḥ nijaghānāśvakarṇena prajaṅghaṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: Saṃpāti, struck by Prajaṅgha with three arrows, slew Prajaṅgha at the forefront of battle with an aśvakarṇa tree.

sanskrit: jambūmālī rathasthas tu rathaśaktyā mahābalaḥ bibheda samare kruddho hanūmantaṃ stanāntare
english: The mighty Jambūmālin, standing in his chariot, enraged, pierced Hanūmān through the chest with a chariot-lance in battle.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ ratham āsthāya hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ pramamātha talenāśu saha tenaiva rakṣasā
english: Then Hanūmān, son of the Wind, mounting that very chariot, quickly crushed Jambūmālin himself with his palm, along with the chariot.

sanskrit: bhinnagātraḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kṣiprahastena rakṣasā prajaghānādriśṛṅgeṇa tapanaṃ muṣṭinā gajaḥ
english: His body pierced by sharp arrows from the swift-handed rākṣasa, Gaja struck Tapana with a mountain peak and then with his fist.

sanskrit: grasantam iva sainyāni praghasaṃ vānarādhipaḥ sugrīvaḥ saptaparṇena nirbibheda jaghāna ca
english: Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, pierced and slew Praghasa—who seemed to be swallowing the armies—with a saptaparṇa tree.

sanskrit: prapīḍya śaravarṣeṇa rākṣasaṃ bhīmadarśanam nijaghāna virūpākṣaṃ śareṇaikena lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Overwhelming the fearsome-looking rākṣasa with a shower of arrows, Lakṣmaṇa slew Virūpākṣa with a single shaft.

sanskrit: agniketuś ca durdharṣo raśmiketuś ca rākṣasaḥ suptighno yajñakopaś ca rāmaṃ nirbibhiduḥ śaraiḥ
english: The invincible rākṣasa Agniketu, and Raśmiketu, and Suptaghna, and Yajñakopa all pierced Rāma with arrows.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ rāmas tu śirāṃsi samare śaraiḥ kruddhaś caturbhiś ciccheda ghorair agniśikhopamaiḥ
english: Then Rāma, enraged, severed in battle the heads of all four of them with four terrible arrows resembling flames of fire.

sanskrit: vajramuṣṭis tu maindena muṣṭinā nihato raṇe papāta sarathaḥ sāśvaḥ purāṭṭa iva bhūtale
english: Vajramuṣṭi, struck down in battle by Mainda with his bare fist, fell to the ground together with his chariot and horses, like a palace tower collapsed.

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamasparśo dvivido 'py aśaniprabham jaghāna giriśṛṅgeṇa miṣatāṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: And Dvivida—whose touch was like thunderbolt and lightning—struck Aśaniprabha with a mountain peak before the eyes of all the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dvividaṃ vānarendraṃ tu drumayodhinam āhave śarair aśanisaṃkāśaiḥ sa vivyādhāśaniprabhaḥ
english: Then Aśaniprabha in turn pierced with arrows like thunderbolts the monkey-lord Dvivida, that fighter with trees, in battle.

sanskrit: sa śarair atividdhāṅgo dvividaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ sālena sarathaṃ sāśvaṃ nijaghānāśaniprabham
english: His body pierced through and through by arrows, Dvivida—overcome with rage—slew Aśaniprabha along with his chariot and horses with a sāla tree.

sanskrit: nikumbhas tu raṇe nīlaṃ nīlāñjanacayaprabham nirbibheda śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ karair megham ivāṃśumān
english: Nikumbha in battle pierced Nīla—who had the luster of a heap of dark collyrium—with sharp arrows, as the sun pierces a cloud with its rays.

sanskrit: punaḥ śaraśatenātha kṣiprahasto niśācaraḥ bibheda samare nīlaṃ nikumbhaḥ prajahāsa ca
english: Then again the swift-handed night-roaming Nikumbha pierced Nīla in battle with a hundred arrows, and laughed.

sanskrit: tasyaiva rathacakreṇa nīlo viṣṇur ivāhave śiraś ciccheda samare nikumbhasya ca sāratheḥ
english: Then Nīla—like Viṣṇu in battle—severed Nikumbha's head in combat with the wheel of Nikumbha's own chariot, and the head of his charioteer too.

sanskrit: vidyunmālī rathasthas tu śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ suṣeṇaṃ tāḍayām āsa nanāda ca muhur muhuḥ
english: Vidyunmālin, standing in his chariot, struck Suṣeṇa with arrows adorned with gold and roared again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ rathastham atho dṛṣṭvā suṣeṇo vānarottamaḥ giriśṛṅgeṇa mahatā ratham āśu nyapātayat
english: Seeing him in his chariot, the foremost monkey Suṣeṇa swiftly brought down the chariot with a great mountain peak.

sanskrit: lāghavena tu saṃyukto vidyunmālī niśācaraḥ apakramya rathāt tūrṇaṃ gadāpāṇiḥ kṣitau sthitaḥ
english: Vidyunmālin the night-roamer, endowed with agility, quickly leapt from the chariot and stood on the ground, mace in hand.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ suṣeṇo haripuṃgavaḥ śilāṃ sumahatīṃ gṛhya niśācaram abhidravat
english: Then Suṣeṇa, the foremost monkey, possessed by rage, seized an immense boulder and charged at the night-roamer.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ gadayā vidyunmālī niśācaraḥ vakṣasy abhijagnānāśu suṣeṇaṃ harisattamam
english: As he came charging, the night-roaming Vidyunmālin quickly struck the best of monkeys, Suṣeṇa, in the chest with his mace.

sanskrit: gadāprahāraṃ taṃ ghoram acintyaplavagottamaḥ tāṃ śilāṃ pātayām āsa tasyorasi mahāmṛdhe
english: Though struck by that terrible mace blow, the incomparable foremost of monkeys hurled that boulder onto Vidyunmālin's chest in the great battle.

sanskrit: śilāprahārābhihato vidyunmālī niśācaraḥ niṣpiṣṭahṛdayo bhūmau gatāsur nipapāta ha
english: Struck by the boulder's impact, Vidyunmālin the night-roamer fell dead to the ground, his heart crushed.

sanskrit: evaṃ tair vānaraiḥ śūraiḥ śūrās te rajanīcarāḥ dvandve vimṛditās tatra daityā iva divaukasaiḥ
english: Thus those heroic night-roaming rākṣasas were ground down in single combat by those heroic monkeys, as the daityas were once by the gods.

sanskrit: bhallaiḥ khaḍgair gadābhiś ca śaktitomara paṭṭasaiḥ apaviddhaś ca bhinnaś ca rathaiḥ sāṃgrāmikair hayaiḥ
english: Struck and pierced with war-headed arrows, swords, maces, lances, tomaras, and paṭṭasas—and with battle-chariots and war-horses—

sanskrit: nihataiḥ kuñjarair mattais tathā vānararākṣasaiḥ cakrākṣayugadaṇḍaiś ca bhagnair dharaṇisaṃśritaiḥ babhūvāyodhanaṃ ghoraṃ gomāyugaṇasevitam
english: —with slain maddened elephants, and with fallen monkeys and rākṣasas, and with broken chariot-wheels, axles, yokes, and poles lying on the earth—the dreadful battlefield was haunted by packs of jackals.

sanskrit: kabandhāni samutpetur dikṣu vānararakṣasām vimarde tumule tasmin devāsuraraṇopame
english: Headless trunks of monkeys and rākṣasas sprang up in all directions in that tumultuous and crushing engagement comparable to the war of gods and asuras.

sanskrit: vidāryamāṇā haripuṃgavais tadā niśācarāḥ śoṇitadigdhagātrāḥ punaḥ suyuddhaṃ tarasā samāśritā divākarasyāstamayābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: The night-roamers, being torn asunder by the foremost monkeys, their bodies smeared with blood, swiftly resumed fierce fighting, longing for the setting of the sun.
